title: Automatically archive Amazon EBS Snapshots with Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager
content:
Automatically archive Amazon EBS Snapshots with Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager Customers use snapshots to capture a point-in-time copy of their data, which can be used to enable disaster recovery, migrate data across regions and accounts, and improve backup compliance. For enterprises using snapshots, it is a common requirement to keep snapshots (which are seldom accessed) for more than 90 days, for compliance purposes. However, the cost of storing these full snapshots for extended periods presents a challenge to IT budget and customers risk non-compliance by deleting snapshots due to budget pressures.
On November 29 2021, Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) announced the availability of Amazon EBS Snapshots Archive, a new storage tier for the long-term retention of Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) snapshots of EBS volumes. Today, we are excited to announce that customers can now leverage Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager – a policy-based lifecycle management solution for EBS Snapshots and EBS-backed Amazon Machines Images (AMIs) available at no additional cost – to create custom policies that automate the archival and retention of EBS Snapshots.
In this workshop, we dive deeper into using Data Lifecycle Manager to automate the creation, archival, and deletion of Amazon EBS Snapshots. Customers that need to keep full, point-in-time snapshots for backup and compliance can now do so by creating ‘set-and-forget’ policies instead of having to manage and maintain complex custom scripts that may lead to data loss because of human errors.

title: Introduction
content: Introduction In this workshop, we will showcase two examples of how you can automate snapshot archival and management with Data Lifecycle Manager, followed by guidance on how you can use the EC2 Console to view the snapshots managed and archived by Data Lifecycle Manager. In the first example, we will create an age-based policy to automate snapshot creation and archival with a single policy schedule. In the second example, we will create a policy to automate snapshot creation and archival using multiple policy schedules. One schedule will keep daily/weekly snapshots in the Amazon EBS Snapshot Standard tier (standard tier), while the other moves snapshots created on a monthly cadence to the EBS Snapshots Archive tier.

title: Launch EC2 instance
content:
Launch EC2 instance  In the AWS Management console, find and select EC2   In the EC2 console, select Instances
 Select Launch instances     In the Lauch instances console
 Enter Name and tags as FCJ Snapshot     For Key pair, you can choose Proceed without a key pair (Not recommended)
 For Networking you can keep the same configuration.    For storage keep the same and then select Launch instance   After launch EC2, select View all instances  Wait about 2 minutes, Status check is 2/2 checks passed  Select the instance created and select Storage, then select Volume  Set the volume tag as FCJ-Volume

title: Preparation
content:
Preparation We will prepare an EC2 to use in the next steps.
 Launch EC2 instance

title: Using a single policy schedule
content:
Use a policy schedule   Access to EC2 console
 Select Lifecycle Manager Select Next step     In the setting step, select Target resources
 Target resource type select Volume Select by tags as FCJ-Volume    Use the default IAM role.  Then select Next   For Schedule configuration.
 In this section, we will configure 1 schedule and 1 policy. Section Schedule name, name it arbitrarily. In the Frequency section, select Daily. Every, choose 1 hour. Starting at at 14:00, you can customize. For *Retention type, choose 30 days.    Select Review policy  Select Create policy  Create lifecycle policy successfully.

title: Use multiple policy schedules
content:
Use multiple policy schedules   Same, but we will create multiple policy schedules with 1 policy lifecycle.
 In the Data Lifecycle Manager console Select Create lifecycle policy     Select EBS snapshot policy
 Select Next     For Target resource, select Volume
 Select by tag: FCJ-Volume Set description as FCJ-DLM-Week policy     Use default IAM Role.
 Select Next.     Go to Schedule configuration step
 For Schedule name, enter optionally. Select Frequency as Weekly Choose the dates of your choice. Choose starting at time as 09:00 For Retention type, select Age and select 180 days    Select Add another schedule   Perform the 2nd Schedule Configuration
 For Schedule name, enter optionally. Select Frequency as Monthly Select Day and Last Choose starting at time as 09:00 For Retention type, select Age and select 1 days    Select Advanced settings   For Snapshot archiving
 Select Archive snapshots created by this schedule Archive snapshots for 90 days Select Review policy    Check again and select Create policy  Finish creating lifecycle policy

title: Review results
content: Review the result.  We review the results by going to the EC2 console and selecting Snapshots  Select a snapshot and view the details.  Select Tags to view detail information about schedule policy and data lifecycle policy

title: Clean up resources
content:
Clean up resources   Deleting lifecycle policy
 Select the policy. Select Actions. Select Delete lifecycle policy.    Confirm deletion.   Choose to delete snapshots.
 Select snapshots related to the lab. Select Actions. Select Delete snapshot.    Confirm deletion.   Implement Terminate EC2 instance.
 Select EC2 instance. Select Instance state. Select Terminate instance.
